first.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4%, signaling a friction point in early product experience rather than a top-of-funnel acquisition problem. Activation messaging (memory_91) directly addresses week-one engagement and first meaningful action—the immediate symptom. While onboarding simplification (memory_86) and signup simplification (memory_31) showed durable gains, those are structural changes requiring longer rollout. Promotional pricing (memory_73) would bleed margin against competitor pressure without addressing why existing users aren't activating. Referral incentives (memory_57) reward established cohorts but don't solve the QoQ decline in new-account activation. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is orthogonal to SMB activation decline. Activation messaging is a contained, fast-cycle lever that can be deployed, measured, and either scaled or pivoted within a week. Verifying memory_86 and memory_91 confirms whether the behavioral mechanisms that drove those wins remain stable and whether messaging is the right causal lever versus structural onboarding friction.
